title: megeszik and megiszik: Eating and Drinking It All Up

sections.title: The same meg-, on eszik and iszik
sections.content: eszik and iszik, from Unit 9, describe eating and drinking in general — Kenyeret eszem doesn't say whether you finish the bread or leave half of it. Add meg-, and megeszik/megiszik say the whole thing gets eaten or drunk, down to the last bite or sip. Because you're finishing one specific, named thing, the object is usually definite, and the verb takes the definite conjugation you already know from befejez and megcsinál.

items.english: I'm drinking a glass of water.

items.spanish: Anna megeszi a levest, és elindul dolgozni.
items.english: Anna finishes the soup, and sets off to work.

sections.content: Compare the objects closely: iszom egy pohár vizet names an indefinite amount — 'a glass of water' — so it takes the plain indefinite verb. megiszom a vizet names the definite, specific water — all of it — so meg- and the definite conjugation arrive together (issza, not iszik, in the 'he/she' form). A finished, definite object almost always calls for both.
